geometry_edits.rationale: Align the courtyard opening to the verified access edge so the ground threshold becomes public and legible.
Increase void depth slightly to improve usable public space and reduce sealed massiness at the base.
Trim the upper terraces so the dominant mass reads as one calm, continuous section rather than stacked fragments.
Delete the twist mutation because it overcomplicates the section and weakens program coherence.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the public threshold by keeping the courtyard/void aligned to the verified access side.
Enlarge the carved void slightly so the ground condition becomes more legible as public space rather than a token notch.
Reduce the dominance of repetitive upper steps to preserve a calmer, more capacity-aware massing hierarchy.
Remove the book/twist complication because it weakens the primary neighborhood-living gesture without adding usable section logic.

rationale: The candidate is coherent as a stepped bar and reads consistently across the four views, so the basic massing grammar is legible. However, it behaves more like an abstract terraced object than a neighborhood-living building with an active ground threshold: the access edge is not strongly articulated as a public seam, the void is present but not clearly public in section, and the upper stepping dominates more than the ground relation. The silhouette is acceptable but somewhat generic, and the book/twist mutations add complication without strengthening program logic. This fails hard program-fit because the visible mass does not convincingly support the required active frontage, public void, and mixed-use ground hierarchy.
